note: Wave-3 answers, Q11 onwards. Q1-Q10 live in otwarchive-facts.json on the Mac branch, which was not on origin when this was written; append these entries to it when the branches meet (same shape: q, answer, sources, quote, implication; 'id' added).
read_from: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive.git (no AO3 page fetched)

facts.q: Do AO3's relative 'Updated' filter and the absolute After/Before dates combine, or does one override the other?
facts.answer: They combine (AND). Both become range filters on revised_at: the relative value is options[:revised_at] handled with the other countable ranges, and date_from/date_to become a second range on the same field. A work must pass both.
facts.quote: [:word_count, :hits, :kudos_count, :comments_count, :bookmarks_count, :revised_at].each do |countable| ... ranges += [date_range_filter, word_count_filter].compact  /  { range: { revised_at: range } }
facts.implication: search-filters 1aq.3: the date section's missing footer can state it as fact.

facts.q: How is a user's subscriptions index paged and ordered, and does it print a total?
facts.answer: Sorted case-insensitively by subscription name in Ruby, then paginated at ArchiveConfig.ITEMS_PER_PAGE (25 in the open-source config; production may override). The page heading names the scope only; no count is printed. type=works/series/users narrows it.
facts.quote: @subscriptions = @subscriptions.to_a.sort { |a,b| a.name.downcase <=> b.name.downcase }  /  @subscriptions.paginate page: params[:page], per_page: ArchiveConfig.ITEMS_PER_PAGE  /  ITEMS_PER_PAGE: 25
facts.implication: home-library 1b.7 (page 1 is not a total), account-hub-reading 1p.3 ('104 total' has no source) and 1p.4 (scopes are type=). Home's carousel shows the alphabetically first page, not the most recent.

facts.q: What does AO3 render past COMMENT_THREAD_MAX_DEPTH, and what does its count mean?
facts.answer: At depth >= 5, if a comment has more than one reviewed reply, AO3 stops recursing and prints one link '(N more comments in this thread)'. N is children_count: every descendant in the nested set, not direct replies. With exactly one reply left it keeps rendering inline ('not if there's just one last measly comment left').
facts.quote: <% if depth >= ArchiveConfig.COMMENT_THREAD_MAX_DEPTH && child_comments.size > 1 %> ... ts("%{count} more comments in this thread", count: comment.children_count)  /  (self.threaded_right - self.threaded_left - 1)/2
facts.implication: browse-workdetail-comments 1f.5 (owner's depth cap; AO3's own is 5 with a one-reply exception); T-254 #7 (a cutoff placeholder's count is a descendant count and belongs in the thread totals).

facts.q: In what order does AO3 page a work's comment threads?
facts.answer: It paginates the commentable's reviewed comments by thread id (Comment.per_page per page). The comments association sets no ORDER, so the order is the database's - insertion (id) order in practice, oldest thread first. 'Newest first' is therefore the last page, reversed.
facts.quote: thread_ids = commentable.comments.reviewed.pluck(:thread).paginate(page: page, per_page: Comment.per_page)  /  has_many :comments, as: :commentable, dependent: :destroy
facts.implication: browse-workdetail-comments 1f.2: the app's newest-first (last page, roots reversed) matches practice; the code does not guarantee the order.

facts.q: What does AO3's 10,000-character comment limit count?
facts.answer: The raw comment_content as submitted, with Rails validates_length_of (Ruby String#length: characters = code points). Sanitizing happens at display time (sanitized_content), not before validation.
facts.quote: validates_length_of :comment_content, maximum: ArchiveConfig.COMMENT_MAX, too_long: ts("must be less than %{count} characters long." ...)  /  COMMENT_MAX: 10000
facts.implication: browse-workdetail-comments 1ba.2: count unicodeScalars, not grapheme clusters.

facts.q: Where do AO3's Blocked users and Muted users pages live, and who may open them?
facts.answer: /users/:user_id/blocked/users and /users/:user_id/muted/users (index). The owner, or an admin with permission. /users/:login/blocked and /muted are not routes, which is why a probe of those 404s.
facts.quote: namespace :blocked do resources :users, only: [:index, :create, :destroy] ...  /  before_action :check_ownership_or_admin, only: :index
facts.implication: account-leftovers 1z.3: both rows can be added with pathSuffix 'blocked/users' and 'muted/users'.

facts.q: Does the drafts page say when each draft will be deleted?
facts.answer: Yes. Drafts renders works/_work_blurb for each unposted work, and the work module adds, for !work.posted?, a caution notice with that draft's own deletion date: created_at + 29 days, formatted date_short_html (Mon 05 Oct 2026). The page-level notice says drafts are saved 30 days from creation.
facts.quote:
<% if !work.posted? %>

<%= t('.draft_deletion_notice_html', deletion_date: date_in_zone(work.created_at + 29.days)) %>

/ draft_deletion_notice_html: This draft will be scheduled for deletion on %{deletion_date}.
facts.implication: account-leftovers 1x.2: 'N days left', 'Created ...' and 'N expiring this week' come from the page already fetched. WritingDraftsView's reason for dropping them is contradicted.

facts.answer: SearchCounts.bookmark_count_for_user: a BookmarkQuery count over all of the user's bookmarks - works, series and external works alike - including private ones when the viewer is the owner. Cached with dashboard_cache_options.
facts.implication: account-hub-reading 1m.3: a count built from parsed work rows is smaller than this and must not replace it.

facts.q: How does AO3 take a work off Marked for Later?
facts.answer: PATCH /works/:id/mark_as_read, which calls Reading.mark_to_read_later(work, current_user, false) and redirects back. The mirror of mark_for_later.
facts.quote: patch :mark_for_later / patch :mark_as_read  /  def mark_as_read ... Reading.mark_to_read_later(@work, current_user, false)
facts.implication: account-hub-reading 1o.3 (the footer's promise) and 1o.4 (the unmark write, owner's call).

facts.q: Which HTML tags survive in AO3 comments?
facts.answer: Sanitize::Config::ARCHIVE's elements: a abbr acronym address b big blockquote br caption center cite code col colgroup details figcaption figure dd del dfn div dl dt em h1-h6 hr i img ins kbd li ol p pre q rp rt ruby s samp small span strike strong sub summary sup table tbody td tfoot th thead tr tt u ul var; details keeps open.
facts.quote: elements: %w[ a abbr acronym ... details ... img ... summary sup ... ]
facts.implication: browse-workdetail-comments 1bf.1: every tray tag survives; img is allowed by AO3 and left out by the board's choice.

facts.q: What do the Inbox heading's counts cover, and which filters does AO3's Inbox support?
facts.answer: @inbox_total and @unread are the user's whole inbox (bad comments removed), unaffected by filters. The list itself is filtered by find_by_filters: read (true/false), replied_to (true/false), and date (ASC/DESC).
facts.quote: @inbox_total = @user.inbox_comments.with_bad_comments_removed.count  /  @unread = ...count_unread  /  replied_to = case filters[:replied_to] when 'true' then true when 'false' then false ...
facts.implication: account-hub-reading 1l.1 (only the awaiting clause is page-scoped) and 1l.2 (Unread = read=false, Awaiting reply = replied_to=false, Replied = replied_to=true are real server filters, so the pill rail can be exact across pages).

facts.q: What order does AO3 use when no sort is sent?
facts.answer: Relevance (_score) for a plain search; revised_at (date updated) for a tag's works list or a collection. Direction defaults to desc.
facts.quote: def default_sort; facet_tags? || collected? ? 'revised_at' : '_score'; end  /  direction = options[:sort_direction].present? ? options[:sort_direction] : 'desc'
facts.implication: Confirms AO3FilterPanel.allowsRelevanceSort = false on Browse's /tags/<t>/works pages and relevance as Search's default.

facts.q: What does AO3's /media page list under each category?
facts.answer: Its five most-used canonical fandoms, by filter_counts.public_works_count (unhidden_works_count when logged in) - a count ranking, not a curated list. Uncategorized shows its five newest fandom tags instead.
facts.implication: browse-workdetail-comments 1g.2: MediaBrowserView's twelve largest fandoms is AO3's own rule at a larger N; its doc comment's 'hand-curated and often stale' is wrong and should be corrected.
